summary: Built 1930 as a Forest Service/CDF lookout in Tulare County; removed 2010, restored, and now displayed at the county fairgrounds, with sources split on whether the tower or only the cab is shown.

facts.design: 60-foot open steel Aermotor tower with a 7x7 observation cab; cab modified in 1960
facts.status_note: Sources disagree on what is shown at the fairgrounds: the 2011 FFLA report says the restored tower was placed there, the Sun-Gazette says the lookout building is on permanent display, and the FFLOS register says only the cabin is on ground-level display

access.note: Displayed at the Tulare County Fairgrounds; visitors were admitted during the county fair in 2011 and 2024. No regular opening hours found.

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection, Tulare Unit (CAL FIRE)

events.note: Built as a cooperative lookout between the Forest Service and CDF

Lifted off its mountain in May 2010 after a four-year effort; taken to CAL FIRE headquarters in Visalia for full restoration

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLOS register says the tower was moved to the Tulare County Fairgrounds in 2010, the year it was lifted off the mountain; the 2011 FFLA report places the restored tower there after restoration, opened in October 2011. The record keeps the 2011 placement event and notes the register's 2010 date.

notes_for_editor: The record's name, 2010 removal, 2011 restoration and fairgrounds location check out. The open question is what is displayed: FFLOS says only the cabin is on ground-level display, while the 2011 FFLA report and the 2017 Sun-Gazette describe the tower or lookout building being displayed, and the 2024 Buck Rock post describes the decommissioned lookout on display; the record's kind 'ground' may reflect this, so it was left unchanged. Height 18.3 m is converted from the register's 60 feet for the tower; the original-site record (us-ca-blue-ridge-tulare-county) lists 22.9 m and was not checked here. No current opening hours found; access is 'public' only in the sense of fair-time display. No photos added.
